Definition right_adjoint_PreservesImageLimit {C D : Category} {F : D ⟶ C} {U : C ⟶ D} (A : F ⊣ U) : @PreservesImageLimit C D U. — the limit-preservation half of the (1) ⇒ (2) direction, at exactly the cone-level notion GAFT consumes (cf. Adjunction/Continuity.v:202 [right_adjoint_preserves_limits : PreservesAllLimits U])

Record SolutionSet {C D : Category} (U : C ⟶ D) (d : D) := { sol_index : Type; sol_obj : sol_index -> C; sol_arr : forall i, d ~> U (sol_obj i); sol_covers {c} (h : d ~> U c) : { i : sol_index & { t : sol_obj i ~> c & fmap[U] t ∘ sol_arr i ≈ h } } }.

statement_record.book: For C locally small and complete, X any category and U : C → X, TFAE: (1) U has a left adjoint; (2) U preserves all limits and satisfies the Solution Set Condition at every object X — a SET of objects (C_i) such that every f : X → UC factors as U(f̄) ∘ φ through some φ : X → UC_i.
statement_record.intree: Theorem GAFT {C D : Category} (U : C ⟶ D) (comp : @Complete C) (cont : @PreservesImageLimit C D U) (sols : forall d : D, SolutionSet U d) : { F : D ⟶ C & F ⊣ U }.

Proof of (2) ⇒ (1): W := Π_i D_i is weakly initial; take V ↣ W the joint equalizer of all endomorphisms of W; V is initial.

Corollary ump_universal_arrows `(c ⟿ F) `(h : c ~> F d) : ∃! g : arrow_obj ~> d, h ≈ fmap[F] g ∘ arrow. — where [Class UniversalArrow (c : C) (F : D ⟶ C) := { arrow_initial : @Initial (=(c) ↓ F); arrow_obj := snd (`1 (initial_obj)); arrow : c ~> F arrow_obj := `2 (initial_obj) }] (line 127), i.e. the initial object of the comma IS the pair (F c, η) with the unit's UMP

Program Definition Comma : Category := {| obj := ∃ p : A ∏ B, S (fst p) ~{C}~> T (snd p); hom := fun x y => ∃ f : (fst (`1 x) ~{A}~> fst (`1 y)) * (snd (`1 x) ~{B}~> snd (`1 y)), `2 y ∘ fmap[S] (fst f) ≈ fmap[T] (snd f) ∘ `2 x; ... |} — at S := =(X) : 1 ⟶ D (Functor/Diagonal.v's [=(c)]) and T := U this is exactly (X ↓ U): objects (C, f : X ~> U C) and arrows g with f' ∘ id ≈ U(g) ∘ f

statement_record.book: For U : C → X and X an object of X, form the comma (X|U) with objects (C, f : X → UC) and arrows g : C → C' satisfying f' = U(g) ∘ f. Then U has a left adjoint F iff for every X the category (X|U) has an initial object, which is precisely (FX, η : X → UFX) with the universal mapping property of the unit.

statement_record.strength_comparison: same for the construction and for the 'if' half: the comma (X ↓ U) is the library's [=(d) ↓ U], the initial object is packaged as [UniversalArrow] whose projections are exactly (FX, η), the UMP is [ump_universal_arrows], and [AdjunctionFromUniversalArrows] (Theory/Universal/Arrow.v:214) verifies that the assembled F is genuinely left adjoint with those arrows as unit. intree-weaker only in that the biconditional is not stated (see gap).

gap: The 'only if' half is never formed: from an adjunction F ⊣ U nothing in-tree produces [@Initial (=(d) ↓ U)] or a [UniversalArrow d U]. The ingredients are one step apart — [adj_univ : f ≈ ⌈g⌉ ↔ ⌊f⌋ ≈ g] and [to_adj_unit : ⌊f⌋ ≈ fmap[U] f ∘ η] (Theory/Adjunction.v:195, 264) give exactly the unique-factorization hypothesis of [universal_arrow_from_UMP] (Theory/Universal/Arrow.v:158), which would then yield the initial object — but that composite appears nowhere (grep 'UniversalArrow' finds only Theory/Universal/Arrow.v, Adjunction/GAFT.v, Construction/Free/Quiver.v:518 and Monad/Lifting.v:445, all producing rather than consuming an adjunction).
